card_summary: The emergence of T-Motion Robotics at the 2026 NAB Show indicates a growing need for precision and flexibility in live signal transport. As we see increased adoption of ST 2110 and NMOS for real-time transport, the demand for robust and reliable robotic camera systems is on the rise. With the ability to seamlessly integrate with existing infrastructure, these systems will be crucial in maintaining signal integrity and frame accuracy in live production environments. In practice, this means engineering teams will need to prioritize robust genlock and synchronization solutions to ensure that robotic camera systems can maintain precise timing and alignment with other live sources, such as 12G-SDI and AES67 feeds. The trade-off here is between the benefits of increased flexibility and the added complexity of integrating multiple signal types and protocols, including SRT and RIST, into a cohesive live production workflow.
body_html:
Why ST 2110 Is Forcing Broadcasters to Rethink Signal Transport

Live signal transport is at a critical juncture, with the increasing adoption of IP-based architectures and the need for lower latency and higher quality signals. The industry is shifting away from traditional SDI and satellite-based systems, and toward more agile and flexible IP solutions. This development represents a significant inflection point for broadcasters, who must now reassess their signal transport infrastructure to meet the demands of modern live production.

What This Development Actually Means

EVS is set to debut its T-Motion Robotics system at the 2026 NAB Show, which promises to revolutionize the way broadcasters transport live signals. The system leverages the latest advancements in ST 2110 technology to provide a highly scalable and flexible solution for live signal transport, with a focus on reducing latency and improving signal integrity.

This announcement sits within the broader context of the industry's shift toward IP-based architectures, driven by the need for greater agility and flexibility in live production. The increasing adoption of ST 2110 and other IP standards is forcing broadcasters to reassess their signal transport infrastructure and adopt more modern and efficient solutions.

Why It Matters for Broadcast Operations

The introduction of T-Motion Robotics and other ST 2110-based solutions will have significant implications for broadcast operations, particularly in terms of CapEx and OpEx costs. Broadcasters will need to budget for the upgrade and replacement of existing SDI and satellite-based systems, as well as the integration of new IP-based infrastructure. This will require careful planning and coordination to minimize disruption to live production workflows.

For regional and national broadcasters, the adoption of ST 2110 will enable significant reductions in transmission costs, as well as lower latency and higher quality signals. This will be particularly beneficial for sports and live event coverage, where high-quality signals are critical to delivering an engaging viewer experience. However, the integration of new IP-based infrastructure will also require careful planning and coordination to ensure seamless integration with existing systems.

For OTT and streaming platforms, the adoption of ST 2110 will require significant changes to their content delivery networks (CDNs) and streaming protocols. This will involve the deployment of new IP-based infrastructure and the adoption of more efficient streaming protocols, such as HLS and DASH. The adoption of ST 2110 will also require careful planning and coordination to ensure that live signals are transported efficiently and reliably to viewers around the world.

Impact by Stakeholder

  • Regional and national broadcasters: Will need to budget for the upgrade and replacement of existing SDI and satellite-based systems, as well as the integration of new IP-based infrastructure. This will require careful planning and coordination to minimize disruption to live production workflows.
